newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech new car import surge continues, report says.
newsitem.headline: Czech new car import surge continues, report says.

text.p: Czech new passenger car imports surged for the second consecutive year in 1996, continuing to erode the dominant market position of local carmaker Skoda Auto a.s., a unit of Volkswagen AG.
A report by the Czech Car Importers Association (SDA) released on Friday showed new passenger car imports last year surged by 61 percent to 71,083 units, after a 39 percent increase in 1995.
The report added that total imports of new light utility vehicles also strenthened, rising 42 percent, year-on-year, to 15,301 units.
The growth of imports allowed foreign car makers to take a further bite out of Skoda's domestic market position, raising its share to 46 percent last year from 39 percent in 1995.
"Members of the assocation managed to fulfil the aim of selling more than 55,000 new passenger cars and 12,000 light utility vehicles," the SDA said in a statement.

The rise in imports, coupled with strong sales of Skoda's Felicia model, which began selling in 1995, boosted overall domestic sales of passenger cars to 153,907 units, an increase of 37 percent year-on-year.
It added the total combined sales of both passenger and light utility vehicles was 174,815, up from 128,701 the previous year.
Skoda remains by far the dominant market player, however, selling 82,734 paasenger cars alone, a 22 percent increase over 1995.
The SDA figures showed that General Motors' unit Adam Opel AG was the largest importer, with combined passenger car and utility vehicle imports of 11,507, up from 7,523 vehicles in the previous year.
Second was Germany's Volskwagen AG with 11,402 in combined imports for 1996 (7,638 in 1995), followed by Ford with a combined 10,690 (6,545 in 1995).
